run.title: steme audit — Baseline and Drift Governance

commit.subject: feat(steme): compute frozen v1 violation fingerprints and dedupe identities
commit.body:
Add the v1 violation fingerprint — sha256 over rule id, source scope, violated
target designation (concept over scope), repo-relative source file and
resolved target, explicitly excluding line numbers and import kind — carried
on every diagnostic and emitted in JSON output. Same-identity edges
deduplicate to one diagnostic. A frozen-value unit test pins the exact hash so
the formula (future SARIF partialFingerprints) can never drift silently; any
change requires a v2 prefix.

commit.subject: feat(steme): add the baseline store and known/new/touched/resolved classifier
commit.body:
Add the baseline contract (seven-field entries, schemaVersion 1, strictly
parsed with named config errors — an expiry field is a rejection, not a
feature), deterministic serialization sorted by ruleId/file/fingerprint for
reviewable diffs, per-app entry scoping, and the drift classifier: exact
fingerprint match is known, same rule and file with a changed fingerprint is
touched (claiming its entry), anything else is new, and unclaimed unmatched
entries are resolved. Pure modules with exhaustive unit tests; no CLI change
yet.

commit.subject: feat(steme): add --write-baseline adoption and --fail-on-new drift enforcement
commit.body:
Wire the baseline into steme audit: --write-baseline runs the full audit and
accepts every current violation of the app into steme-baseline.json (exit 0,
refusing with exit 2 if the app is already covered — accepting more drift is
the governance command's job), and --fail-on-new compares against the register
and fails only when new drift exists. Known violations are summarized, never
itemized; new and touched are itemized with state tags and a
known/new/touched/resolved drift line in both renderings. Missing or malformed
baselines and contradictory flags are cannot-run refusals (exit 2). Committed
completions and CLI reference regenerated.

commit.subject: feat(steme): add steme governance accept-drift and the baseline lifecycle harness
commit.body:
Accepting drift becomes an explicit governance operation: steme governance
accept-drift runs the audit, keeps exactly-matched baseline entries with their
original acceptance metadata, adds every unmatched current violation with a
mandatory --reason, and prunes resolved debt — deterministic, byte-stable
output, exit 0 always (a governance write, never a policy verdict). A
disposable-copy E2E harness proves the whole adoption lifecycle: adopt,
protect, new drift fails, identity survives line moves and type flips, touched
is signaled without failing, resolved is pruned, refusals exit 2, and foreign
apps' entries survive every write byte-identically.
